observations: Two nearly identical photos show a large blue plastic drum with a lid.
The lid has two white screw caps and four metal retaining brackets.
An embossed up-arrow symbol and green paint marks are visible on the drum wall.
Other blue drums and a blue jerrycan appear in the background.
A watermark reads "SAIVET NIGERIA ENTERPRISE" and "POSTED ON JIJI".
No brand, model, capacity, or resin code is readable in either photo.
The seller sent only words, no new photo; their claim of self-testing is not visual evidence.

claims.evidence: No food-grade marking or resin code visible; seller's word is not proof.

claims.claim: used only once for clean water
claims.evidence: Usage history cannot be determined from still photos; seller's claim is not proof.
No obvious cracks are visible, but remote photos cannot rule out hairline cracks.
A leak test cannot be performed from photos; seller's self-test is not verifiable remotely.
Photo 0 and photo 1 show the lid with both caps and metal straps in place.

risks.risk: Drum is not food grade and previously held chemicals or non-food substances.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of any embossed resin code, recycling symbol, or manufacturer marking on the drum wall.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a standard used chemical-grade drum

risks.risk: Hidden cracks or leaks at seams, bungs, or around the lid.
risks.proof: Video showing the drum filled with water and inspected for seepage.

risks.risk: Lid gaskets or cap seals are missing or perished.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the underside of both white caps showing the seals.

proof_requests: Close-up of any embossed resin code or markings on the drum wall.
Video of the drum filled with water to check for leaks.
Close-up of the underside of both white caps to confirm gaskets.
response.reason: The item is clearly a used blue plastic drum and can be priced at its worst case without further proof; the seller's verbal assurance adds no verifiable evidence.
